note: Original station IDs with licensed Kevin MacLeod recordings (CC BY 4.0). Unique channel-specific stories, researched against linked sources; fact citations are editorial references, not endorsements.

channels.name: Ad Break
channels.tag: A little word from yesterday.

fact.fact: Energizer's giant Bunny balloon needed 84 miles of thread and size-98 feet. The battery-ad mascot became an airborne craft project on an absurd scale.

channels.name: Rerun Alley
channels.tag: Your usual seat is still here.

fact.fact: Dick Van Dyke's famous ottoman opening was filmed in about four minutes. Carl Reiner requested a second version where he dodged it, keeping viewers guessing.
fact.credit: PBS American Masters / John Rich interview

channels.name: Late Night
channels.tag: One more before bedtime.

fact.hook: The Pencil That Could Only Erase
fact.fact: Johnny Carson had pencils specially made with erasers on both ends for The Tonight Show. Even his desk stationery had its own comedy routine.

channels.name: Big Prize
channels.tag: No purchase necessary. Just a comfy chair.

fact.fact: On a plane, Julann Griffin proposed giving contestants the answers. Her husband Merv tested it with 5,280; the question was feet in a mile.

channels.name: Brit TV
channels.tag: Put the kettle on.

fact.fact: John Cleese based Basil Fawlty on real hotelier Donald Sinclair, whose behavior included correcting guests' table manners. A disastrous hotel stay became a classic sitcom.

channels.name: PBS
channels.tag: Stay curious. Stay a little longer.

fact.hook: His Mother Was the Wardrobe Department
fact.fact: The Smithsonian's Mister Rogers cardigan still carries his mother's name inside: Nancy knitted it herself, just as she made sweaters he wore on television.
fact.credit: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

channels.name: Y2K WB
channels.tag: Back when the evening had a theme song.

fact.hook: All That Talking Filled Extra Pages
fact.fact: Gilmore Girls burned through 77–78-page scripts; its showrunner said the crew shot nine or ten pages daily to keep up with all that conversation.

channels.name: Porchlight
channels.tag: Small towns. Big feelings.

fact.hook: The Moose Had a University Job
fact.fact: The moose strolling through Northern Exposure's opening credits was Morty, a Washington State University research animal with a second career in television.

channels.name: Prime Time Tapes
channels.tag: The whole night, all over again.

fact.hook: A Fake Ending Guarded the Real One
fact.fact: To protect Newhart's surprise finale, a fake ending sent his character to heaven. Suzanne Pleshette stayed hidden until the secret final scene was filmed.

channels.name: Strange Tales
channels.tag: Something is a little off. Stay tuned.

fact.fact: The Twilight Zone's famous theme joined two separate pieces from CBS's music library. Marius Constant had written them as short fragments, never as that signature tune.

channels.name: Sitcom Gold
channels.tag: A familiar room. A familiar laugh.

fact.fact: Lucy Ricardo's baby arrived on television the same day Lucille Ball delivered Desi Jr. Her real birth was coordinated with the broadcast through a planned cesarean.
fact.credit: Television Academy / Desi Arnaz Jr. interview

channels.name: Spooky '90s
channels.tag: The truth can wait through this bumper.

fact.fact: In a 2018 survey, half the women familiar with Dana Scully said the X-Files character increased their interest in science, technology, engineering or mathematics.
fact.credit: Geena Davis Institute / 2018 Scully Effect study

channels.name: Order Now
channels.tag: Operators are probably on a tea break.

fact.fact: Ron Popeil said developing his Olive Oil Fryer consumed 30,000 pounds of turkey; much of the testing food went to firefighters and homeless people.
fact.credit: Ron Popeil interview / University of Illinois Alumni Association

channels.name: Paint Along
channels.tag: A little room for a happy accident.

fact.fact: Bob Ross got a perm to save money on haircuts, then grew tired of it. By then, his curly-haired portrait had become the company logo.

channels.name: Variety Hour
channels.tag: A little bit of everything, with applause.

fact.fact: Elvis's first Ed Sullivan Show appearance happened without Ed Sullivan. Recovering from a serious car crash, the host left Charles Laughton to introduce television history.
fact.credit: The Ed Sullivan Show official archive

channels.name: Saturday Toons
channels.tag: Cereal optional. Cartoons essential.

fact.fact: The village built for Robin Williams's Popeye movie was not demolished. Its colorful wooden houses survived in Malta and became a tourist attraction.

channels.name: Cartoon Vault
channels.tag: Fresh out of the ink bottle.

fact.hook: Those Earrings Used to Be Ears
fact.fact: Betty Boop began as a dog-like character. As the studio made her human, her floppy canine ears evolved into the hoop earrings everyone recognizes.

channels.name: Scooby & Friends
channels.tag: The gang will be right back.

fact.fact: Scooby-Doo's name traces to Frank Sinatra's scat singing at the end of Strangers in the Night. A crooner helped name television's famously frightened dog.

channels.name: Toon Toys
channels.tag: Some assembly required. Watching is easy.

fact.fact: Peter Cullen based Optimus Prime on his older brother Larry, a Vietnam Marine veteran whose advice was to make heroism compassionate, rather than merely loud.

channels.name: '90s Kids
channels.tag: Your after-school seat is saved.

fact.hook: The Sponge Began in a Classroom
fact.fact: SpongeBob's ancestor was Bob the Sponge, created while Stephen Hillenburg taught marine biology at an ocean institute. The cartoon's creator really did teach sea life.

channels.name: After School
channels.tag: Homework can wait eight seconds.

fact.fact: Bill Nye spotted a camera-calibration post and proposed turning it into a sundial for Mars, giving a spacecraft instrument an unexpectedly ancient second job.
fact.credit: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day

channels.name: Adult Swim
channels.tag: A very reasonable place to get weird.

fact.fact: After Dave Willis erased Dana Snyder's voicemail audition, Snyder returned to the same restaurant, repeated his drinks, and recorded it again at three in the morning.
fact.credit: Dave Willis interview / Inverse oral history

channels.name: Puppet Show
channels.tag: A little felt. A lot of personality.

fact.fact: Cookie Monster's ancestor, the Wheel Stealer, began in a snack commercial with teeth. Before Sesame Street, he also appeared for IBM and on Ed Sullivan.
fact.credit: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

channels.name: Caped Crusaders
channels.tag: Even heroes take a tiny breather.

fact.hook: Three Weeks to Build the Batmobile
fact.fact: The 1966 Batmobile started as a futuristic Lincoln show car. George Barris's team had just three weeks to turn the Futura into Batman's ride.

channels.name: Drive-In
channels.tag: Park here. The next picture is coming.

fact.fact: Richard Hollingshead tested drive-in movies with a projector on his car hood, a bedsheet between trees, and lawn sprinklers standing in for bad weather.

channels.name: After Dark
channels.tag: Keep the lights low.

fact.hook: Noir, with a side of sausage.
fact.fact: The Third Man's haunting zither music came from Anton Karas, whom director Carol Reed discovered playing in a tiny beer-and-sausage restaurant.

channels.name: Creature Feature
channels.tag: Our monsters need a moment.

fact.fact: Night of the Living Dead's gruesome menu was surprisingly ordinary: Bosco chocolate syrup supplied the blood, while a local butcher donated roasted ham for the flesh.

channels.name: Chiller Hosts
channels.tag: A little fright between friends.

fact.fact: Before Elvira, Cassandra Peterson was a Vegas showgirl. She credits Elvis Presley with urging her to leave and try singing, helping redirect her career.

channels.name: Silent Screen
channels.tag: No dialogue. Plenty to say.

fact.fact: For Steamboat Bill, Jr., Buster Keaton stood beneath a real falling house front. He said its window cleared each shoulder by just two inches.
fact.credit: Buster Keaton interview / The New Yorker

channels.name: Laugh Track
channels.tag: Save a little room for the next laugh.

fact.fact: Harold Lloyd performed Safety Last!'s dizzying climbing stunts after losing his right thumb and index finger. A specially made glove concealed the missing digits.

channels.name: Kung Fu Theater
channels.tag: Stretch your remote-control hand.

fact.fact: Enter the Dragon opens with Bruce Lee sparring against Sammo Hung. Another future superstar appears among the fighters later: a still-unknown Jackie Chan.

channels.name: Frontier
channels.tag: Rest your boots. Stay a spell.

fact.fact: The classic Western tumbleweed, Russian thistle, reached the United States in contaminated flax seed from Russia. Its American invasion began in South Dakota in 1873.

channels.name: Private Eye
channels.tag: The next clue is coming up.

fact.hook: The hat was the illustrator's idea.
fact.fact: Conan Doyle never specifically called Sherlock Holmes's hat a deerstalker. Illustrator Sidney Paget supplied the detective's famous look in drawings accompanying the original stories.

channels.name: Christmas Movies
channels.tag: The season is whenever you tune in.

fact.fact: Movie snow once used white-painted cornflakes. For It's a Wonderful Life, effects artists developed quieter foam-based snow so footsteps would not drown out the dialogue.

channels.name: Showstoppers
channels.tag: A little intermission. A lot of sparkle.

fact.hook: It almost faced the other way.
fact.fact: West Side Story began as East Side Story: a Romeo-and-Juliet musical about Catholic and Jewish families on Manhattan's Lower East Side, before the concept changed.

channels.name: Anime Station
channels.tag: One more episode? We understand.

fact.fact: Akira's animators did not settle for an ordinary paint box. Its 327-color palette included fifty colors mixed specifically for that single film's production.

channels.name: Dubbed Anime
channels.tag: Same adventure. Familiar voices.

fact.hook: Three shows wearing one trench coat.
fact.fact: Robotech was assembled from three separate Japanese series: Macross, Southern Cross and Mospeada. New scripts turned their unrelated stories into one continuing American saga.

channels.name: Retro Anime
channels.tag: Big eyes. Bigger adventures.

fact.fact: Astro Boy creator Osamu Tezuka treated his recurring characters as actors, casting familiar faces in different stories and even imagining how much they were paid.

channels.name: AMV Hour
channels.tag: A little picture. A little rhythm.

fact.fact: Daft Punk's Discovery became Interstella 5555, a feature-length anime adventure with no dialogue. The songs and animation tell the story of an abducted alien band.

channels.name: Kaiju Theater
channels.tag: Please keep the model city tidy.

fact.hook: Godzilla is secretly a bass player.
fact.fact: Godzilla's original roar was not an animal recording. Composer Akira Ifukube dragged a resin-coated leather glove along a double bass's loosened strings to create it.

channels.name: Mecha Hangar
channels.tag: All systems comfy.

fact.hook: The toy company picked the paint.
fact.fact: Gundam's bright colors were not purely a creative choice. Creator Yoshiyuki Tomino said the toy-company sponsor required the robot to use red, white and blue.

channels.name: Magical Girls
channels.tag: A little sparkle goes a long way.

fact.hook: Venus got there before the Moon.
fact.fact: Sailor Venus was a solo heroine before Sailor Moon existed. Naoko Takeuchi first gave Minako her own adventures as Sailor V, guided by Artemis.

channels.name: Power Level
channels.tag: Power up. Settle in.

fact.fact: Akira Toriyama struggled to name Master Roshi's signature attack. His wife suggested Kamehameha; he liked how silly and appropriate it sounded, and kept it.
fact.credit: Akira Toriyama interview / Ian Kelley translation

channels.name: OVA Vault
channels.tag: Straight from the shelf to your screen.

fact.hook: Chicago was not just a backdrop.
fact.fact: Gunsmith Cats' animators traveled to Chicago to research the real thing, visiting gun shops, police facilities and the Police Academy instead of inventing every detail.

channels.name: Toonami Tapes
channels.tag: Your transmission will resume shortly.

fact.fact: Toonami's robot host TOM shares his voice with Cowboy Bebop's Spike Spiegel. Both are performed by Steve Blum, who also voices several versions of Wolverine.

channels.name: Gridiron
channels.tag: Your seat on the fifty is saved.

fact.fact: Portsmouth's star Dutch Clark missed the NFL's first playoff. He had already returned to his other job: coaching basketball at Colorado College.

channels.name: Rink Side
channels.tag: Keep your stick on the ice.

fact.fact: Detroit’s octopus tradition began with seafood-shop brothers in 1952. Its eight arms represented the eight playoff victories then needed to win the Stanley Cup.

channels.name: Ringside
channels.tag: Stay in your corner. We will be right back.

fact.fact: Heavyweight champion Jack Johnson was also an inventor. He patented an improved wrench in 1922, giving him another way to deliver a powerful grip.

channels.name: Pit Lane
channels.tag: A quick pit stop. Then back to it.

fact.fact: After winning Le Mans in 1967, Dan Gurney shook his champagne and sprayed the people nearby. That spontaneous celebration became a motorsport podium ritual.

channels.name: Skate & Surf
channels.tag: Catch the next one.

fact.fact: Neoprene wetsuit pioneer Hugh Bradner was a Manhattan Project physicist. He began improving diving gear as a weekend project while working at Berkeley.

channels.name: Sweatin'
channels.tag: Grab some water. You earned it.

fact.fact: Jane Fonda says her Workout helped sell VCRs: people finally had a tape they wanted to play repeatedly, rather than watch just once.

channels.name: Hoops
channels.tag: A tiny timeout. Then more basketball.

fact.fact: There is no available video footage of Wilt Chamberlain’s 100-point game. The NBA’s record scoring night left fans without a replay.

channels.name: Ballpark
channels.tag: Stretch a little. The next pitch is coming.

fact.fact: Chicago’s Disco Demolition Night blew up records between games. Fans invaded the field, and the White Sox forfeited game two.

channels.name: Video Jukebox
channels.tag: Leave a little room on the mixtape.

fact.hook: This trophy actually went to space.
fact.fact: MTV’s Moonman wasn’t only pretending to be an astronaut. A Video Music Award statue flew aboard the Russian space station Mir in 1996.

channels.name: Soul Train
channels.tag: Keep a little groove in your evening.

fact.hook: Four hundred dollars started the party.
fact.fact: Don Cornelius made the Soul Train pilot with $400 of his own money. Its name came from a road show he created for local high schools.

channels.name: Headbangers
channels.tag: The volume knob is yours.

fact.fact: After losing fingertips in a factory accident, Tony Iommi melted plastic washing-up bottles into replacement fingertips so he could keep playing guitar.

channels.name: Jazz Club
channels.tag: Your table is still here.

fact.hook: The bent trumpet was an accident.
fact.fact: Dizzy Gillespie’s trumpet was accidentally bent during a party. He liked its strange new sound and had later trumpets deliberately built with the same bend.

channels.name: Encore
channels.tag: One more for the road.

fact.fact: Jimi Hendrix was supposed to close Woodstock around midnight. Delays pushed his performance to Monday morning, when roughly 40,000 people remained from the enormous crowd.

channels.name: Ephemera
channels.tag: Small films. Big time capsules.

fact.fact: Kodak traced mysterious film spots to radioactive cardboard. Trinity-test fallout had contaminated the river water used by the Indiana mill making its packaging.

channels.name: Duck & Cover
channels.tag: A curious little window into yesterday.

fact.fact: Las Vegas hotels promoted views of nuclear tests. Casinos hosted dawn parties, served atomic cocktails, and advertised detonation times as a tourist attraction.

channels.name: Home Movies
channels.tag: Somebody remembered to bring a camera.

fact.fact: Regular 8mm film started twice as wide. You filmed one side, flipped the spool, filmed the other, then the lab slit it lengthwise and joined the ends.

channels.name: Computer Chronicles
channels.tag: Please wait. Nostalgia is loading.

fact.hook: The bug is still in the book.
fact.fact: In 1947, Harvard engineers found a moth in their computer and taped it into the logbook. That literal bug is now in the Smithsonian collection.

channels.name: Mission Control
channels.tag: All stations, stand by for wonder.

fact.hook: The Moon landing survived a reboot.
fact.fact: Apollo 11’s overloaded guidance computer repeatedly restarted during descent. It preserved essential landing tasks while dropping unnecessary radar jobs, letting the astronauts continue toward the surface.

channels.name: Wild Kingdom
channels.tag: A little room for the wild.

fact.fact: Wombats produce cube-shaped poop inside their intestines. Researchers found that alternating stiff and stretchy regions help sculpt the corners before anything leaves the animal.

channels.name: TV Dinner
channels.tag: Something good is on.

fact.fact: Before television, Julia Child worked for the OSS. One assignment placed her with a rescue-equipment unit developing shark repellent, long before her famous French recipes.

channels.name: Strange Signals
channels.tag: The signal is strange. The seat is comfy.

fact.fact: The first U-2 became airborne at Area 51 during a high-speed taxi test. Its pilot had intended to stay on the ground that day.

channels.name: Slow TV
channels.tag: Nothing to rush. Nowhere to be.

fact.fact: The original televised Yule Log was filmed at New York’s Gracie Mansion. A stray spark damaged an antique rug after the crew removed the protective screen.

channels.name: Arcade
channels.tag: Insert comfy chair. Press start.

fact.fact: Pong’s bar prototype was reported broken after two weeks. The fault wasn’t electronics: its milk-carton coin catcher had become jammed with quarters.

channels.name: Starbase
channels.tag: Your home port between adventures.

fact.hook: The Enterprise had a bad side.
fact.fact: The original Enterprise filming model had exposed wiring on one side. Its glamorous screen appearance hid a much rougher backstage side.

channels.name: Hyperdrive
channels.tag: Next stop: somewhere else entirely.

fact.hook: Vader's lungs came from a dive shop.
fact.fact: Darth Vader's breathing began with sound designer Ben Burtt breathing through a scuba regulator. He put the microphone inside the regulator to capture it.

channels.name: Riff Raff
channels.tag: The couch has room for one more.

fact.hook: Crow was partly a bowling pin.
fact.fact: Crow T. Robot's homemade anatomy includes a plastic bowling pin, a lacrosse mask and Tupperware. The wisecracking robot really was assembled from ordinary stuff.

channels.name: Atomic Age
channels.tag: Yesterday imagined a very big tomorrow.

fact.hook: This toy came with actual uranium.
fact.fact: The Gilbert U-238 Atomic Energy Lab gave children uranium ore, radioactive sources and a Geiger counter. It was sold as an educational toy in 1950-51.

channels.name: Deep Space
channels.tag: A little farther from the everyday.

fact.hook: We sent someone's brainwaves into space.
fact.fact: Voyager's Golden Record carries music, greetings and a recording of Ann Druyan's brainwaves. Humanity's message to the stars includes the electrical activity of a human mind.

channels.name: World of Tomorrow
channels.tag: The future used to look like this.

fact.hook: EPCOT was supposed to have residents.
fact.fact: Walt Disney's original EPCOT was a working city where people would actually live. The theme park came later; the city of tomorrow was never built.

channels.name: Cliffhangers
channels.tag: Do not touch that dial. Seriously.

fact.fact: The 1948 live-action Superman serial switched to a cartoon Superman for flying effects. An actor could play the Man of Steel; drawings handled the airborne work.

channels.name: Subspace 97
channels.tag: Set phasers to comfy.

fact.fact: Nichelle Nichols planned to leave Star Trek. Then Martin Luther King Jr. told her how much Uhura mattered, and she decided to stay.
